overview: Small pastes (<64 KB) go straight into a KV store (DynamoDB) with a TTL attribute; large ones spill to S3. Expiry is handled by the store itself.

estimation.result: Read-heavy traffic benefits from cache/CDN independently of durable storage.
estimation.implication: Inline small values only within store limits; use object storage for large bodies.

entityDetails.purpose: Paste metadata and either an inline body or object-store pointer.
accessPatterns: Create a random paste key; point-read metadata and body.
constraints: Check expires_at at read time; random IDs are not a substitute for access control when privacy is required.

apiDetails.purpose: Create an immutable paste with optional expiry.
apiDetails.rationale: Validate size and atomically publish metadata after body storage; clean up orphaned objects.
Cache TTL and CDN behavior must respect expires_at; physical deletion may run later.

steps.title: Browser → LB → Paste Service → Paste KV store
steps.explanation: Store a small body inline with expires_at; large bodies use the object-store spill path.

steps.title: Paste Service → Paste bodies
steps.explanation: Only large pastes write an immutable object and metadata pointer.

steps.title: Browser → CDN → LB → Paste Service → Redis
steps.explanation: Use a cached value only if its application expiry remains valid.

steps.title: Paste Service → Paste KV store
steps.explanation: Read inline data or a pointer; reject expired items even if the store has not physically deleted them.

failureCases.scenario: Body upload succeeds but metadata insert fails
failureCases.handling: Garbage-collect unreferenced objects after a grace period; retries create or reuse a clearly identified paste. Always check expiry even if the object still exists.

alternatives: Use object bodies plus metadata for large pastes and cheap retention. Use inline KV items for small pastes with a spill path above item limits. Both enforce expiry on reads before background deletion.
